section: SCCS/1625/20, Overall safety assessment of benzophenone-3 (p. 82)
hazard: The SCCS identified concerns regarding the potential endocrine-disrupting properties of benzophenone-3 (BP-3). The available evidence from in silico modelling, in vitro tests, and in vivo studies was considered inconclusive. The assessment also identified safety concerns associated with the use of BP-3 at 6% as a UV filter in body creams and sunscreen sprays.
opinion: Benzophenone-3 can be considered safe under specific conditions of use, depending on the cosmetic product and concentration. The SCCS considers its use as a UV filter up to 6% safe in face creams, hand creams, and lipsticks, but not in body creams or sunscreen sprays at that concentration. For body creams and sunscreen sprays, the maximum safe concentration is 2.2% when BP-3 is used only as a UV filter, or 1.7% when an additional 0.5% is used to protect the cosmetic formulation. Although the evidence does not conclusively establish BP-3 as an endocrine-disrupting substance, further investigation is warranted. Environmental safety was not assessed.
conditions: BP-3 is considered safe up to 6% as a UV filter in face creams, hand creams, and lipsticks, and up to 0.5% when used to protect cosmetic formulations. In body creams, propellant sprays, and pump sprays, the maximum safe UV-filter concentration is 2.2%, provided that no additional 0.5% is used to protect the formulation. If BP-3 is also used at 0.5% for formulation protection, the UV-filter concentration should not exceed 1.7%.
source_quote: The use of BP-3 as a UV-filter up to a maximum concentration of 6% in sunscreen products, either in the form of body cream, sunscreen propellant spray or pump spray, is not safe for the consumer.
